articles.title: Netflix corta cerca de 1.000 empregos  | G1
articles.standfirst: Redução atinge 6% do quadro de funcionários e afeta áreas de tecnologia, produto, jurídico e recursos humanos, informa o Wall Street Journal.
articles.summary: Redução atinge 6% do quadro de funcionários e afeta áreas de tecnologia, produto, jurídico e recursos humanos, informa o Wall Street Journal.
articles.body:
Evento da Netflix — Foto: REUTERS/Francis Mascarenhas

A Netflix vai demitir cerca de 6% de sua força de trabalho, o que representa aproximadamente 1.000 vagas. Esta é a maior rodada de cortes da empresa de streaming desde 2022, informou o jornal Wall Street Journal nesta quarta-feira (14).

Segundo o WSJ, a decisão foi comunicada aos funcionários por meio de um e-mail enviado na manhã de quarta-feira pelos co-presidentes executivos da companhia, Greg Peters e Ted Sarandos.

A maior parte das demissões ocorrerá nas equipes de produto, tecnologia, recursos humanos e no departamento jurídico.

No final do ano passado, a empresa contava com cerca de 16 mil funcionários em tempo integral. A companhia não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário feito pela agência de notícias Reuters.

Os cortes ocorrem em um momento de intensa concorrência pela atenção dos usuários em um mercado de mídia cada vez mais consolidado.

Para diversificar suas fontes de receita, a Netflix tem expandido sua atuação além do modelo de assinaturas, realizando investimentos em publicidade, programação ao vivo e jogos.

O cenário de consolidação do setor inclui movimentos recentes de concorrentes diretos. No início deste ano, a Netflix perdeu a disputa pelos ativos de estúdio e streaming da Warner Bros Discovery para a Paramount Skydance.

A Paramount concluiu a aquisição da Warner Bros neste mês por 110 bilhões de dólares , formando a Skydance, uma gigante de mídia que reúne um portfólio de estúdios de cinema e notícias.

A operação reúne marcas como Warner Bros., Paramount Pictures, HBO Max, Paramount+, CNN e CBS e coloca sob o comando de David Ellison um grupo que terá cerca de US$ 80 bilhões em dívidas.

A nova companhia passa a se chamar Skydance e terá suas ações negociadas na Bolsa de Nova York sob o código "SKYD". A mudança ocorreu nesta terça-feira, quando os papéis da empresa combinada deixaram de ser negociados na Nasdaq.

O acordo encerra uma das maiores disputas recentes pelo controle de ativos de Hollywood. A Paramount Skydance venceu uma concorrência que também envolveu a Netflix e atraiu o interesse de outras empresas, como a Comcast.

A fusão junta os estúdios responsáveis por franquias como Harry Potter, Batman, Missão: Impossível e Top Gun, além de serviços de streaming e grandes redes de televisão. A empresa passa a atuar em cinema, televisão, streaming e jornalismo.

articles.title: Dollar advances to highest since May 2025 on Fed hike views
articles.summary: The dollar strengthened to the highest level in over a year as hot US inflation reading pushed traders to add to bets that the Federal Reserve will raise int...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- The dollar strengthened to the highest level in over a year as hot US inflation reading pushed traders to add to bets that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates.

The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index surged Wednesday past its November high. The gauge rose as much as 0.4% to the highest level since May 2025. US consumer prices advanced at the fastest pace in five months on rising fuel costs, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data.

"Hotter than expected CPI has given a boost to the Dollar this morning as traders price in further tightening from the Fed," said Andrew Hazlett, a foreign-exchange trader at Monex Inc.

The dollar has surged nearly 3% for the four-week period ending Oct. 9 to post its longest winning streak since early 2025. The rally has been fueled by traders' rate predictions since the Fed raised rates for the first time in three years last month. That move has been followed by hawkish remarks from central bank officials. The market is now pricing in more than 90 basis points of rate increases in the US.

Elevated oil prices due to the ongoing war in Iran and heightened concern over fiscal and political risks in France have boosted demand for the haven currency. The war has also been lifting global yields. While central bank policymakers in other major countries are also gearing to raise borrowing costs to stem price growth, not all economies can handle the same amount of rate hikes as the US through September.

A widening interest-rate gap is favoring the dollar, with many strategists on Wall Street rethinking their outlook for the US currency. Speculative traders boosted their bullish stance on the dollar in the week through Oct. 6, holding more than $35 billion in wagers tied to the dollar rising, Commodity Futures Trading Commission data show.

articles.title: US inflation accelerates to 3.7% in September as gasoline prices surge
articles.summary: US consumer inflation accelerated in September as a surge in gasoline prices and firmer underlying price pressures added to the cost-of-living burden for
articles.body: US consumer inflation accelerated in September as a surge in gasoline prices and firmer underlying price pressures added to the cost-of-living burden for American households ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.The consumer price index (CPI) rose 3.7 per cent year-on-year in September, up from 3.4 per cent in August, the US Labor Department said on Wednesday. On a monthly basis, consumer prices increased 0.6 per cent, compared with a 0.4 per cent rise in the previous month.The annual inflation rate was slightly above economists' expectations of 3.6 per cent, according to a Reuters poll, while the monthly increase was in line with forecasts.The latest figures reflect the impact of higher energy costs following the US-Israeli war with Iran, which began in late February and disrupted oil and gas supplies. Rising costs have added to concerns over affordability, a key issue ahead of the midterm elections, in which President Donald Trump's Republican Party is seeking to retain control of Congress.Gasoline prices drive inflationGasoline prices were a major contributor to the monthly increase in consumer prices, rising sharply in September. US Energy Information Administration data showed gasoline prices climbed 7.1 per cent during the month, while the Labor Department's CPI report recorded a 9.1 per cent increase.Higher fuel costs have also pushed up expenses across other sectors, including transportation and travel. Airfares rose 1.2 per cent in September and were up around 22 per cent from a year earlier, while hotel prices increased 2 per cent over the month.Rising fuel and transportation expenses have also increased costs for businesses, raising the risk that companies will pass some of the additional burden on to consumers through higher prices for goods and services.Grocery prices offered some relief, declining 0.1 per cent in September, although they remained 1.8 per cent higher than a year earlier.Core inflation also picks upUnderlying price pressures remained firm even after excluding volatile food and energy components. Core CPI rose 2.6 per cent in September from a year earlier, compared with 2.4 per cent in August.On a monthly basis, core inflation increased 0.3 per cent, matching the previous month's rise. Price increases across a range of goods and services suggest that inflationary pressures extend beyond the energy sector.Economists have also pointed to strong investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure and data centres as a factor pushing up the cost of semiconductors, computer equipment and electronic devices.“The report was worse than expected,” Bill Adams, chief US economist at Fifth Third Bank, said in a note to clients, adding that price increases were widespread across durable goods, nondurable goods and services.What it means for Federal ReserveThe inflation data could complicate the Federal Reserve's decisions on interest rates as policymakers weigh persistent price pressures against the impact of tighter monetary policy on economic growth.The Fed raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points last month to a range of 3.75 per cent to 4 per cent, marking its first rate increase in three years. It has indicated that further increases could follow if inflation remains elevated.Financial markets had assigned a roughly 22 per cent probability of another rate increase at the Fed's October 27-28 meeting before the September CPI report, according to CME Group's FedWatch Tool.However, some economists expect policymakers to hold rates steady at the upcoming meeting and assess further economic data before deciding on another increase. Higher borrowing costs can help moderate demand and slow price increases, but they cannot directly address supply disruptions caused by geopolitical conflicts.The latest inflation figures come as the cost of living remains a major concern for American voters ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.The September inflation report is also important for millions of Americans receiving Social Security benefits. The annual cost-of-living adjustment for 2027 is based on inflation data for urban wage earners and clerical workers during the third quarter of 2026 compared with the corresponding period a year earlier.The Senior Citizens League has projected a 3.5 per cent increase in Social Security benefits for 2027, up from the 2.8 per cent adjustment for 2026. The Social Security Administration is expected to announce the official adjustment later on Wednesday.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: United Airlines adds Starlink Wi-Fi — and a potential loyalty perk to poach Delta, American flyers
articles.summary: United Airlines is upgrading its fleet to high-speed Starlink Wi-Fi. Now, it's making the case for members of competitor loyalty programs to switch to Mileag...
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

United Airlines is rolling out high-speed Starlink Wi-Fi on flights and inviting travelers to try the service with a valuable new MileagePlus status match.

United ( UAL ) has spent much of this year upgrading its flights to have Starlink access. A recent analyst note from Sheila Kahyaoglu at Jefferies said Starlink is already available on just under 600 United aircraft. That includes about 300 regional jets and 300 mainline aircraft.

That's an increase from the over 450 aircraft United reported in its July earnings. Earlier this year, Ankit Gupta, United's chief air operations officer, said close to 1,000 aircraft would have Starlink by the end of 2026.

United says it expects 50% of its mainline fleet to have Starlink by the end of this year, and 100% to be equipped with high-speed Wi-Fi by the end of 2027.

The quick rollout puts United ahead of other major U.S. airlines in switching to high-speed internet in-flight. American Airlines ( AAL ) is also upgrading to Starlink, though it will begin installing the service in 2027. Delta Air Lines ( DAL ) offers free Wi-Fi to SkyMiles members on flights and is making "meaningful enhancements" to that service this year, but will begin upgrading to Amazon Leo (another high-speed service) in 2028.

In the meantime, United is using its advanced Wi-Fi service to entice travelers to switch from American and Delta to its MileagePlus loyalty program via a status match offer. Until Oct. 15, elite-status members of either competing airline can get a status match with United lasting through Jan. 31, 2028.

Here's what to know about United's Starlink availability and MileagePlus perks for those who take advantage of the match.

On flights with Starlink Wi-Fi enabled, United MileagePlus members can connect for free. Without a MileagePlus account, travelers won't be able to access the Starlink connection.

United's first wide-body Starlink flight across the Atlantic was on June 22, from Newark to London. The airline said passengers could expect the service on routes between its major hubs in the U.S., including Newark, Washington D.C., Houston, and San Francisco, and popular international destinations — London, Paris, Tokyo, and more.

While travelers won't know the Starlink status of their flights at booking, they can find out whether they're on an upgraded plan when checking in for a flight.

For flights that don't yet have Starlink, United still offers Wi-Fi options. Access costs $8 or 800 miles for United MileagePlus members and $10 for everyone else. That's for domestic and short-haul international flights; prices for other international flights can vary.

As it rolls out Starlink access — and amid an ongoing dispute between SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Delta CEO Ed Bastian — United is making its faster Wi-Fi a selling point for frequent travelers who may be looking for a change.

Through Oct. 15, travelers with elite status on Delta or American Airlines can get their status matched within the United MileagePlus program. The status match will last through Jan. 31, 2028.

Members can submit their request on United's website by completing a form and uploading proof of status within either the Delta SkyMiles or American AAdvantage loyalty program. That request will get approved within three days and remain active for 90 days.

Within the 90-day period, members must also meet a certain spending threshold on United or United Express flights to maintain the status match until January 2028. The required spend depends on the status being matched:

Delta SkyMiles or American AAdvantage status

Platinum Medallion / AAdvantage Platinum Pro

Diamond Medallion / AAdvantage Executive Platinum

Anyone with MileagePlus status is eligible for free Starlink Wi-Fi on eligible United flights, even standard members. But increasing status tiers also offer additional benefits when flying United. Here's a closer look at some of the perks of each tier:

Premier Silver: 1 free checked bag, Group 2 boarding, 2 more miles earned per dollar on flights, free day of departure upgrades when available

Premier Gold: 2 free checked bags, Group 1 boarding, 3 more miles earned per dollar on flights, free upgrades starting 48 hours before departure

Premier Platinum: 3 free checked bags, Group 1 boarding, 4 more miles earned per dollar on flights, free upgrades starting 72 hours before departure, and 40 PlusPoints (which you can use to request upgrades on United and eligible partner flights)

Premier 1K: 3 free checked bags, priority pre-boarding, 6 more miles earned per dollar on flights, free upgrades starting 96 hours before departure, free drink and snack when flying Economy, and 280 PlusPoints

United MileagePlus credit card holders to earn more miles on flights starting April 2

You'll now get more miles on United flights with a United MileagePlus card. Here's how to decide if it's right for you.

articles.title: Canada's Fairfax to buy 60.2% stake in IDBI Bank for Rs 53,000 crore; largest FDI in an Indian bank
articles.summary: Canada-based Fairfax Financial Holdings is set to acquire a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank for approximately Rs 53,000 crore ($5.5 billion).
articles.body: Canada-based Fairfax Financial Holdings is set to acquire a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank for approximately Rs 53,000 crore ($5.5 billion). The transaction would rank as the largest foreign investment in an Indian bank. It marks a big step forward in India's long-pending efforts to privatise state-owned banking assets.The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has approved M/s 10955230 Canada Inc, a subsidiary of Fairfax, as the strategic buyer for the combined stakes held by the government and Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC). The government will sell its 30.48 per cent holding for around Rs 26,620 crore, while LIC will divest its 30.24 per cent stake for approximately Rs 26,440 crore.The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs' approval brings to a close a process that has stretched over nine years. Valuation disagreements had repeatedly complicated the sale. In February 2026, initial bids from Fairfax and Emirates NBD came in below the government's undisclosed reserve price, forcing a pause in the process. The bidding exercise was subsequently revived, and the revised offers were placed before the cabinet committee for consideration.Fairfax, led by Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa, will pay Rs 81 per share. This is above the benchmark fair value of Rs 75.99 arrived at by two independent valuation agencies, according to an official statement.Biggest foreign investment in an Indian bankThe proposed sale is the biggest transaction in the banking sector and a major development in the prolonged effort to privatise IDBI Bank and reduce government ownership of commercial enterprises.The transaction is expected to be completed before the end of FY27. Once the deal goes through, the government will withdraw its representatives from IDBI Bank's board.Emirates NBD's acquisition of a 60 per cent stake in RBL Bank was valued at $3 billion. The Fairfax-IDBI Bank transaction would also exceed MUFG Bank's purchase of a 20 per cent stake in Shriram Finance for Rs 39,618 crore. That deal was described as the largest cross-border investment in India's financial-services sector, but the IDBI Bank transaction is larger by around Rs 13,000 crore.The proposed acquisition is also significantly bigger than Sumitomo Mitsui's $2 billion deal for Fullerton India Credit and PayU's $4.7 billion acquisition of BillDesk, which was the largest financial-services transaction of its period.The disinvestment process was initiated in 2022 but suffered a setback earlier this year when the initial bids received were lower than the government's reserve price.Following the announcement on Wednesday, IDBI Bank shares rose 9.07% to close at Rs 90.44 apiece on the BSE.Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman described the deal as a "milestone", saying "having supported the bank's recovery, we are now enabling its next phase of growth through the infusion of Foreign Direct Investment while retaining a minority stake"."This will not only strengthen the banking ecosystem but also help banking services surpass global benchmarks. It reinforces that India's growth story is strong, its economy is resilient, and the government's commitment to reform is unwavering," she added.Regulatory approvals neededThe transaction cannot be completed until it receives the necessary regulatory clearances. These include approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), which will carry out a "fit and proper" assessment, as well as clearances from the Competition Commission of India (CCI) and other statutory authorities.Before the sale can be finalised, Fairfax will have to establish its credentials with the RBI and submit a roadmap outlining how it intends to meet the regulator's requirements.The company will also be required to make an open offer to public shareholders, unless the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) grants a waiver.Under RBI regulations, promoters are permitted to hold a maximum stake of 26 per cent in a bank.Fairfax will have up to 15 years to meet this requirement, Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) Secretary Arunish Chawla said. The promoter will also be subject to a five-year lock-in period, he added.Fairfax already owns a 40 per cent stake in Kerala-based CSB Bank. Following the IDBI Bank acquisition, it will have to either merge the two lenders or exit its investment in CSB Bank, which is based in South India.Chawla said the incoming promoter would be required to preserve IDBI Bank's existing name, brand and customer relationships for a minimum of three years.Addressing concerns among employees, he said they had no reason to worry. The transfer of management, he added, had been discussed with all stakeholders.LIC, meanwhile, will be required to reduce its holding in IDBI Bank from 19 per cent to 15 per cent within two years.The IDBI Bank deal could mark a turning point for India's banking industry by establishing a potential model for privatising other state-owned lenders, where government ownership continues to be predominant.It will also offer a test of whether investors are willing to take control of a large Indian bank while navigating stringent regulatory conditions and the challenges involved in running a financial institution.The government, however, has described the proposed divestment as a "strategic restructuring". It has maintained that the Centre and LIC will together retain a 34 per cent stake in the bank.The sale would come after the Tata Group's takeover of Air India, completed in January 2022. Tata had won the bid for the national carrier in October 2021 with an offer of Rs 18,000 crore, comprising Rs 2,700 crore in cash and the assumption of Rs 15,300 crore in debt.You use AI every day. articles.title: Bending Spoons stock soars on new Berkshire Hathaway investment
articles.summary: Bending Spoons stock soared as much as 54% in morning trading on Wednesday after the Italian tech company said Berkshire Hathaway will invest another $330 mi...
articles.body:
Bending Spoons stock ( BSP ) soared as much as 54% in morning trading on Wednesday after the Italian tech company said Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK-B ) will invest another $330 million in it.

The stock hit $58 per share at one point in the morning, just shy of its intraday record of $58.94 set on Aug. 11, before settling back to a gain of about 38% around 11 a.m. ET. If the gain holds, Wednesday would be the stock's best day since its July 1 market debut.

Trading volume passed 9.8 million, more than four times the stock's three-month daily average, according to Yahoo Finance data.

Berkshire is buying the new stock in a private placement at $33 per share, about 13% below Tuesday's close, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Wednesday.

The deal lifts Berkshire's stake to 4%, the company said. Berkshire invested $600 million in Bending Spoons at its initial public offering in July. The IPO was priced at $29.

The stock is up around 80% from its IPO price, giving Bending Spoons a market value of about $33 billion.

Bending Spoons said it will use the money for general corporate purposes and new acquisitions. It expects the deal to close in the fourth quarter. Neither the announcement nor the filing included a comment from Berkshire.

"For decades now, Berkshire Hathaway has been among the finest and most respected capital allocators in the world, and is a longstanding inspiration for Bending Spoons," CEO and co-founder Luca Ferrari said in the announcement .

"Bending Spoons continuously evaluates M&A opportunities, and our pipeline remains strong," said co-founder Francesco Patarnello, who leads the company's acquisitions. He said the investment "will further enhance our financial flexibility and ability to pursue attractive acquisitions."

Bending Spoons buys established tech companies and overhauls how they run. Its businesses include AOL, Vimeo, Evernote, WeTransfer, Eventbrite, and Airtable, which it finished acquiring on Sept. 4. On Sept. 10, it agreed to buy Miro at an enterprise value of $1.355 billion.

Wednesday's surge follows another jump a week earlier. The stock closed up 24% on Oct. 7 without an obvious catalyst. It gave back part of that gain but closed Tuesday more than 14% above its Oct. 6 close.

articles.title: Federal watchdog says 9 large US banks denied service to customers over political or religious views
articles.summary: A federal banking watchdog determined that nine banks' sweeping internal guidelines lacked objective, risk-based criteria, effectively shutting out legitimat...
articles.body:
The Comptroller of the Currency says the nation's nine largest banks denied financial services to customers based on their political, religious, or social beliefs, according to a regulatory review released Wednesday.

The OCC reviewed nearly 100,000 complaints and received approximately 50,000 documents from JPMorgan Chase Bank, Bank of America, Citibank, Wells Fargo Bank, U.S. Bank, Capital One, PNC Bank, TD Bank, and BMO Bank regarding their policies, procedures, practices, and individual customer decisions.

The federal banking watchdog determined that the banks' sweeping internal guidelines lacked objective, risk-based criteria, effectively shutting out legitimate customers and businesses based on ideological leanings rather than financial risk.

The OCC said its findings reveal a systematic effort within the banking sector to restrict access for politically sensitive industries through both public and nonpublic policies.

Federal regulators found that lenders restricted certain sectors' access to financial services, including oil and gas exploration; coal mining; firearms or ammunition manufacturing or distribution; construction or operation of detention facilities; and the manufacturing, distribution or online retail of tobacco or e-cigarettes.

The Trump administration has voiced growing concerns over "de-banking" and the use of the financial system to achieve social and political objectives.

"Today's report provides irrefutable evidence that the nation's largest banks have denied, debanked, and discriminated against customers and lawful businesses," said Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan Gould. "Americans should have access to financial services regardless of their beliefs, affiliations, or political views. "

All nine banks report having reassessed the role of reputation risk in decisions to accept or terminate new customers, according to the OCC's report. Several banks said they had minimized reliance on reputation risk, and bank employees now must consider it in the context of other financial or business consequences, including credit risk, money laundering and terrorist financing risk.

The Bank Policy Institute, a lobbying group that represents the banks, said in a statement in reaction to the report, "We support efforts to establish clear and consistent standards that promote access while maintaining sound risk management, including the administration's recent efforts to prioritize supervisory attention on material financial risk and rather than reputational risk."

articles.title: India remains top Russian crude buyer in September despite 29% fall in imports since July
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India remained the world's largest destination for Russian crude oil in September, although imports fell nearly 29 per cent from July levels as
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India remained the world's largest destination for Russian crude oil in September, although imports fell nearly 29 per cent from July levels as Chinese refiners stepped up purchases and tightened the availability of Russian supplies, according to ship-tracking data from Kpler.India imported around 1.82 million barrels per day (bpd) of Russian crude in September, compared with China's 1.49 million bpd. Indian imports had peaked at 2.6 million bpd in June and 2.57 million bpd in July before declining to 2.02 million bpd in August.The moderation comes amid US pressure on countries buying Russian oil, including through tariffs and sanctions. However, analysts say the decline in India's purchases also reflects supply constraints and growing competition from China, rather than being solely a response to Washington's actions."The recent moderation in India's Russian imports is not simply a response to US tariff pressure; tighter availability and stronger competition from China have also played an important role," said Sumit Ritolia, senior manager (modelling) at Kpler.Chinese refiners have increased their purchases of Russian crude in recent months, partly because of reduced access to Iranian oil, adding to competition for available supplies.Based on cargoes currently being tracked, Kpler expects India's Russian crude imports to remain broadly stable at around 1.8 million to 1.9 million bpd in October.US pressure over Russian oil, but a diesel deal with MoscowIndia's continued reliance on Russian crude comes amid Washington's efforts to discourage purchases of Russian energy. US President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 into law in September. The legislation authorises tariffs of up to 100 per cent on imports from countries buying Russian oil, but gives the president discretion over whether and how to apply them. India and China are among the major buyers potentially affected.However, Washington's own approach to Russian energy has also shifted in response to rising fuel costs.On October 9, Trump announced an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin under which Russia would supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel to US and global markets, followed by additional shipments. The Trump administration also temporarily eased US sanctions on Russian fuel to facilitate the arrangement, which was aimed at increasing supplies and containing prices ahead of the November midterm elections.The move nevertheless drawn criticism from Ukraine and some European leaders, who argue that purchases of Russian energy could provide Moscow with additional revenue during its war against Ukraine.Meanwhile, alongside Russian supplies, Venezuelan crude has regained a place in India's import mix this year after remaining largely absent in recent years. Shipments began accelerating from April, according to Kpler.Venezuela exported around 250,000 bpd of crude to India in August and 257,000 bpd in September. The US remained the larger destination, receiving approximately 452,000 bpd in August and 563,000 bpd in September.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Apple retakes $5 trillion market cap, only second company to eclipse milestone number
articles.summary: Apple's market cap crossed the $5 trillion mark on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Apple's ( AAPL ) market capitalization once again crossed the $5 trillion mark on Wednesday, just months after it first touched the threshold in late July.

It's been just under a year since Apple's market cap topped $4 trillion in October 2025. The company's stock price is up roughly 26% year to date and nearly 40% over the past 12 months.

Apple stock climbed more than 1% Wednesday.

The milestone comes a little more than a month after John Ternus took over as Apple CEO from Tim Cook , who stepped down on Sept. 1, a day after Apple debuted its HomeView smart home hub amid a renewed effort to grab share in the smart home market.

Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) currently dominate that space .

Apple has also benefited from strong iPhone sales throughout 2026 on the back of a renewed upgrade cycle.

The company has also finally fleshed out its AI strategy after investors heavily criticized the iPhone maker for initially falling behind in the AI race and struggling to catch up.

Apple unveiled its Apple Intelligence platform at its WWDC event in 2024, but the company delayed a number of features, leaving Wall Street to question Apple's ability to compete with rivals, including Google and Microsoft ( MSFT ).

But the company has since won a reprieve.

It has partnered with Google to use some of the search giant's AI models and rolled out a number of major updates to Apple Intelligence, including its Siri AI, though the software is still in beta.

And then there's the iPhone Duo foldable, which, at $1,999, could boost the iPhone line's average selling price and the company's bottom line. Apple is also preparing to launch its first touch-screen MacBook and revamped iPads later this month, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman .

But Apple is also working to contend with the ongoing memory and storage shortage, which has forced it to raise prices on its iPhones, iPads, and Macs, driving fears that sales could take a hit.

articles.title: ‘Not benefiting anyone’: Traders urge Rahul to rethink SIR protests amid festive season, cite business losses
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Traders’ associations have urged Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to reconsider the ongoing protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR)
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Traders’ associations have urged Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to reconsider the ongoing protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and issues concerning Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that demonstrations and road blockades in the national capital are hurting businesses ahead of Diwali.Representatives of trade bodies said traders stock up on goods and often take loans ahead of the festive season, relying on increased sales to meet annual expenses. They claimed that disruptions were keeping customers away, restricting market access and affecting deliveries, with small traders bearing the brunt.Ajay Gupta, a member of the National Traders Welfare Board, said “I humbly request the Leader of the Opposition, Shri Rahul Gandhi ji, to reconsider the agitation currently underway, as it is not benefiting anyone; instead, it is creating an atmosphere of anarchy,” he said. “We are not opposed to the act of protesting itself ... but it should be done in a manner that causes no harm to the common man and creates no obstacles for us traders in running our businesses,” he added.Meanwhile, Ghanshyam Das Goyal of the Dal and Besan Millers Association said traders from areas around Delhi usually visit the capital to purchase stocks for Diwali, but the disruptions had discouraged them from coming. Prakash Purgal of the Bangalore Wholesale Cloth Merchant Association also urged Rahul to pursue dialogue instead of road blockades, warning that closures during the Dussehra-Diwali and wedding season could hurt small businesses. “The Navratri festival is currently underway. Traders from areas surrounding Delhi usually come to the city to purchase stock for the Diwali season; however, due to the commotion you have stirred up, people have stopped visiting Delhi,”Prakash Purgal, representing the Bangalore Wholesale Cloth Merchant Association, also urged Rahul to ensure that protests did not lead to road blockades during the festive season. He said Dussehra, Diwali and the wedding season were crucial for traders, who had begun to see a recovery after a prolonged period of business difficulties.Warning that road blockades could force small traders to shut their shops, Purgal called for disputes to be resolved through dialogue.“Please consider this carefully: whatever issues need to be discussed should be addressed through dialogue, rather than by blocking roads and spoiling the festive spirit of Dussehra and Diwali,” he said.Several trade bodies from Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Karnataka and Kerala submitted representations on October 12 and 13, seeking steps to ensure that protests do not obstruct commercial activity during the festive season.The traders’ appeal comes amid an intensifying INDIA bloc campaign against the Election Commission’s functioning under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The Opposition has demanded Kumar’s resignation, scrapping of the SIR exercise and restoration of deleted voter names, alleging irregularities in the revision process. It has also called for a return to ballot papers instead of electronic voting machines (EVMs), restoration of pre-SIR electoral rolls for future elections and an effective appeals mechanism for voters excluded from the rolls. articles.title: AI infra startup Modal raises $750 mn at $15.7 bn valuation
articles.summary: Modal Labs raises $750m led by Accel at a $15.7bn valuation, topping $1bn annualized revenue run rate as demand surges for AI infrastructure and sandboxes.
articles.body: BENGALURU: AI infrastructure startup Modal Labs, co-founded by Delhi-raised computer scientist and Olympiad gold medallist Akshat Bubna, has raised $750 million that values the company at $15.7 billion. The fundraise comes as the five-year-old company crossed $1 billion in annualised revenue run rate, fuelled by growing demand for infrastructure that powers AI applications.The latest valuation is more than three times the $4.6 billion Modal was valued at in May this year, when it raised $355 million in a Series C round. The company’s valuation has risen more than 14-fold since September 2025, when it was worth $1.1 billion.Accel led the latest round, with Kleiner Perkins joining as an investor. Existing backers Menlo Ventures, General Catalyst, Redpoint, Lux Capital and Bain Capital Ventures also participated, the company said on Wednesday.Modal said usage of its platform had tripled in the five months since its previous funding round, while the business had grown more than 15-fold year-on-year. Its annualised run rate, which reflects the pace of revenue extrapolated over a year rather than revenue earned in the preceding 12 months, has climbed from about $300 million in May to over $1 billion.Founded in 2021 by Bubna and Swedish engineer Erik Bernhardsson, Modal provides computing infrastructure that allows companies to develop, run and scale AI applications without having to manage their own servers or computing hardware. Its platform now draws capacity from more than 20 cloud providers, allowing developers to access computing power as demand rises or falls.One of Modal’s fastest-growing businesses is Sandboxes, a product that allows AI agents to execute code in isolated environments. Launched in 2023, the product alone has reached a $300 million annualised run rate, the company said. Modal claims it has launched nearly three billion such environments to date and can support up to one million running simultaneously.The surge reflects growing adoption of AI coding agents, which need computing environments to execute programs, test results and carry out tasks. Modal said its infrastructure is used by companies including DoorDash, Cognition, Ramp and Runway, as well as robotics firms Physical Intelligence, Generalist AI and 1X.Modal is also expanding its products for AI model training and inference, the process of running trained models to generate outputs. Its latest launches include tools for training models across multiple machines and new capabilities for running AI applications.Bubna, who became the first Indian student to win gold at the International Olympiad in Informatics in 2014, previously told TOI that conventional cloud infrastructure was not designed for the demands of modern AI.In an interview last year, Bubna explained that Modal’s approach was to build its own software systems rather than depend on tools originally created for older computing applications. “One of the things programming competitions teach you is that most things are pretty solvable. You get used to solving harder problems,” he said at the time.The company has also expanded its workforce sharply. Modal had around 70 employees when Bubna spoke to TOI last year. It now employs more than 200 people across New York, San Francisco and Stockholm.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Groww Q2 profit up 54% to Rs 725 cr
articles.summary: Groww Q2 net profit jumps 54% to Rs 725 crore; revenue up 44% to Rs 1,541 crore as margin lending grows and US stock investing is tested.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Online investment platform Groww’s net profit rose 54% from a year earlier to Rs 725 crore for the September quarter. Its revenue rose 44% to Rs 1,541 crore, with margin lending and commodity derivatives contributing a larger share.Sequentially, however, net profit fell 1.4% from Rs 735 crore in the June quarter, while revenue dipped 0.5% from Rs 1,549 crore.The company is also testing a US stock investing product, co-founder and CEO Lalit Keshre told analysts. He described it as a very early test and said there was no fixed timeline for a launch. “The feedback is really good from the customers,” he said, adding that Groww would continue refining the product based on their responses.Equity derivatives revenue fell 14.3% from the previous quarter. Groww attributed most of the decline to market adjustments following Sebi’s introduction of a closing auction system in August, which changed how closing prices are determined for certain stocks. The segment remained its biggest income contributor, but its share fell to 44.8% from 56.9% a year earlier.Management said proposed changes to derivatives settlement could help normalise trading activity. It cautioned that volumes would also depend on factors such as market volatility.Meanwhile, Groww’s outstanding margin trading loan book grew to Rs 4,351 crore from Rs 1,668 crore a year earlier. The facility allows customers to borrow funds to buy shares.Chief financial officer Ishan Bansal said Groww had tightened its lending policies and was examining exposure to individual stocks across the industry, alongside its own positions.“We have to start looking at the industry level book as well,” he said. Groww is excluding some stocks from its approved lending list or requiring higher margins. In some cases, Bansal said, it finances only 20% of the value, limiting its exposure if prices fall sharply.Expenses rose 29% to Rs 556 crore. Technology costs increased because of more trading days, greater use of AI and higher computing costs. Groww also incurred Rs 13 crore in one-time client reimbursements following an operational issue at a third-party market infrastructure institution. Management said delayed files on an expiry day had caused the issue.Marketing spending fell sequentially because IPL-related expenses incurred in the June quarter did not recur. Management said it typically spends Rs 400–500 crore annually on growth, with spending adjusted to market conditions.IPO activity helped Groww add 11 lakh new transacting users during the quarter. Total customer assets across its platforms rose 46% to Rs 3.9 lakh crore.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: CPI inflation live updates: Prices rose 3.7% in September
articles.summary: Inflation continued its climb in September.
articles.body: Inflation heated back up in September, with the Consumer Price Index coming in at a hotter-than-expected 3.7% annual reading, driven primarily by surging fuel prices. But even “core” inflation, which excludes energy and food, increased more than economists projected, rising 2.6% annually, up from 2.4% in August.The latest figures complicate the Federal Reserve’s task of bringing down inflation to its 2% target. Traders had widely been expecting the Fed to hold interest rates steady at its meeting later this month, but odds of a hike are now rising on the September data.
